title: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay

analysis.tldr: A deterministic compiler turns passive desktop activity into compact, auditable episodic memory frames, avoiding an LLM in the memory-construction path.
analysis.problem: Personal agents need persistent memory of what a user actually did on a computer, but raw screen/activity logs are too verbose and LLM summaries can be lossy, expensive, and hard to audit.
analysis.core_idea: Compile low-level screen activity into typed Activity Frames keyed by application/site, time, input volume, and evidence pointers, while separating measured facts from optional inferred semantics.

memory_design.write: Deterministically segment passive screen-activity events into bounded frames and retain pointers to supporting evidence.
memory_design.organize: Store a chronological sequence of typed activity frames with coverage/gap information and a strict measured-versus-inferred tier boundary.
memory_design.read: Expose compact frames to downstream agents and replay/pattern tools instead of injecting raw activity rows or free-form summaries.
memory_design.update_forget: Frames can be deterministically recompiled as source events change; the paper does not introduce a semantic forgetting policy.

analysis.evidence: Across eight evaluated days, Activity Frames reach 98.4% QA accuracy with the strongest reported Claude settings, versus 82.1-91.1% for raw rows and 66.1-80.4% for LLM summaries; the compiler is reported at 68 ms and the representation is much smaller than raw activity.
analysis.why_it_matters: The interesting design point is not another retrieval algorithm: it shows that some high-volume agent memory can be compiled deterministically before any model sees it, improving provenance and reducing construction cost.
limitations: Evaluation is a single-user, single-machine study with one capture engine.
Screen presence is an imperfect proxy for user attention and intent remains largely unobserved.
The evaluation covers one model family and a short observation period, so generalization to long-lived multi-device agents is unknown.
